mainTopic: Who may teach children, trades that involve women, and how to choose a trade for one's son, with תורה above all.
overview: The amud opens with the last words of the previous discussion, הכל לשם שמים. A new משנה then says a רווק and a woman should not teach young children. The גמרא explains that the worry is the children's parents who visit the school, not the children themselves, because ישראל are not suspected of משכב זכר. It also shows that רבי אלעזר's rule includes a married man whose wife does not live with him. A second משנה warns against trades that involve constant dealings with women. It then gives several views on choosing a trade: רבי מאיר says to pick a clean, easy trade and pray, since a living depends on merit. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and אבא גוריא add their own views, and רבי נהוראי says to teach only תורה, proving his point from פסוקים and from אברהם אבינו. The גמרא lists trades done with women, explains why their workers are not appointed מלך or כהן גדול, and lists ten bad traits of the bloodletter. It ends with בר קפרא's advice to teach a clean, easy trade and asks which trade that is. רב יהודה's answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing line: everything is for the sake of Heaven
steps.stepSummary: The previous discussion ends with the principle that these actions are permitted when done for the sake of Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everything is for the sake of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the discussion before our משנה. It closes that topic by saying these actions are allowed when done purely for the sake of Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion dealt with showing affection to close family members. This line explains that when there is no improper intent, only pure family love, these actions are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of Heaven, with pure intentions

phrases.english: Everything is for the sake of Heaven.
phrases.notes: This closes the discussion before our משנה. Acts of family affection with pure intent are allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier sugya before the new משנה begins.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Actions done with pure intent, for the sake of Heaven, are permitted.

steps.title: The משנה: who may not teach children, and related precautions
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids a רווק or a woman to teach children. רבי אלעזר extends this to a man without a wife. רבי יהודה adds rules about herding animals and sharing a blanket, and the חכמים permit these.
steps.simpleTranslation: An unmarried man should not teach children, and a woman should not teach children. רבי אלעזר says: even a man who has no wife should not teach children. רבי יהודה says: an unmarried man should not herd animals, and two unmarried men should not sleep under one blanket. The חכמים permit these things.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה lists precautions meant to keep people away from situations that could lead to sin. It starts with who may be a teacher of young children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case says a רווק and a woman should not teach children. רבי אלעזר adds a man who has no wife, and the גמרא will soon ask exactly what he means. רבי יהודה goes further with herding animals and sharing a blanket, but the חכמים disagree and permit both.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a teacher of young children

steps.confusionAlert: סוֹפְרִים here does not mean 'scribes.' It means being a teacher of young children.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
An unmarried man should not teach children.
phrases.notes: Literally 'teach scribes.' It means teaching young children their first lessons.

phrases.english: And a woman should not teach children.
רבי אלעזר says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אִשָּׁה לֹא יְלַמֵּד סוֹפְרִים.
phrases.english: Even one who does not have a wife should not teach children.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לֹא יִרְעֶה רַוּוֹק בְּהֵמָה,
phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: an unmarried man should not herd animals,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יִישְׁנוּ שְׁנֵי רַוּוֹקִין בְּטַלִּית אַחַת,
phrases.english: and two unmarried men should not sleep under one blanket,
but the Sages permit it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A רווק and a woman may not teach children. רבי אלעזר adds a man without a wife. רבי יהודה forbids a רווק to herd animals and two רווקים to share a blanket, and the חכמים permit these.

steps.title: Why may a bachelor not teach? A first suggestion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the משנה's rule and suggests the concern might be the children themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? If you say it is because of the children...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a רווק may not teach children. It offers a first guess, which it is about to test in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first guess is that the teacher might sin with the children themselves. The sentence stops here because the גמרא is setting up a challenge to this guess, which comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be tested)

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason?
If you say it is because of the children,
phrases.notes: This means a worry that he might sin with the children themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the משנה's first rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a רווק may not teach children.

steps.title: Challenge: ישראל are not suspected of such sins
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records the חכמים telling רבי יהודה that ישראל are not suspected of משכב זכר or of sinning with animals, so the children cannot be the concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: they said to רבי יהודה, ישראל are not suspected of משכב זכר or of sinning with an animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first guess with a ברייתא. If ישראל are not suspected of this sin, the concern cannot be the children themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the חכמים use this principle to argue against רבי יהודה's rules about herding and sharing a blanket. The same principle knocks out the idea that a bachelor teacher is suspected with the children.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: they said to רבי יהודה:
phrases.notes: 'They' are the חכמים who argued with him in our משנה about herding and the blanket.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְשְׁדוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל מִשְׁכַּב זְכוּר
phrases.english: Jews are not suspected of relations between men
nor of sinning with an animal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion raised in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the bachelor's restriction is because of the children themselves.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since ישראל are not suspected of משכב זכר, there is no basis to fear the teacher will sin with the children.

steps.title: The real reason: the children's parents
steps.stepSummary: A רווק may not teach because of the children's mothers, and a woman may not teach because of the children's fathers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: a bachelor is restricted because of the children's mothers, and a woman because of the children's fathers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reason. The worry is the parents who come to the school, not the children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mothers who come by could be alone with an unmarried male teacher. Fathers who come by could be alone with a female teacher. This reason fits with the principle that ישראל are not suspected of משכב זכר.
steps.whatToRemember: The restriction on a רווק or a woman teaching children is about the parents who visit, not about the children themselves.

phrases.english: Rather: a bachelor, because of the children's mothers.
A woman, because of the children's fathers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reason with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the original reason with a different one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The concern was the children themselves.
steps.terutzMaskana: The concern is the parents of the opposite gender who visit the teacher.

steps.title: What did רבי אלעזר mean by 'no wife'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי אלעזר means only a man with no wife at all, or also a married man whose wife does not live with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: even one who does not have... They asked: does he mean one with no wife at all, or perhaps one whose wife does not live with him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רבי אלעזר's words in the משנה and raises a question about what exactly he meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man with no wife at all would already sound like the רווק of the first ruling. So maybe רבי אלעזר is adding a married man whose wife lives elsewhere. The גמרא wants to know which case he meant.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר אַף מִי שֶׁאֵין כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: רבי אלעזר says: even one who does not have, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points back to his full words in the משנה: 'a wife should not teach children.'

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
does he mean one who has no wife at all,
or perhaps one whose wife is not living with him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה to clarify רבי אלעזר's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אלעזר's rule covers a married man whose wife does not live with him.

steps.title: Answer: even a married man whose wife lives elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that even a man who has a wife, if she does not live with him, should not teach children.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: even one who has a wife, but she is not living with him, should not teach children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא. רבי אלעזר's rule includes a married man whose wife does not live with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אף ('even') shows that the rule reaches past an unmarried man. A man whose wife lives elsewhere is also restricted, since he is in a similar situation when the mothers visit.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר, even a married man should not teach children if his wife does not live with him.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: אַף מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ וְאֵינָהּ שְׁרוּיָה אֶצְלוֹ
phrases.english: Even one who has a wife, but she is not living with him,
should not teach children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר's rule includes a married man whose wife does not live with him.

steps.title: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה about a bachelor herding
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's rule from the משנה, that a bachelor may not herd animals. It then brings a ברייתא where the חכמים tell him Jews are not suspected of משכב זכר or of sinning with animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יהודה says a bachelor may not herd animals, and so on. A ברייתא teaches: The חכמים said to רבי יהודה, 'Jews are not suspected of relations between males or of relations with an animal.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי יהודה's rule in the משנה. It shows from a ברייתא that the חכמים disagreed with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה worried that a bachelor alone with animals might sin with them. The חכמים answer that ישראל are not suspected of this sin, so no special rule is needed. This is the same answer the חכמים gave in step 4, now used against his rule about herding.
steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא already showed up in step 4. There it answered the worry about children. Here the גמרא brings the same words again to answer רבי יהודה's rule about herding.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר לֹא יִרְעֶה כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: [A bachelor] may not herd, etc.
It is taught: They said to Rabbi Yehuda:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְשְׁדוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל מִשְׁכַּב זְכוּר
phrases.english: Jews are not suspected of relations between males
nor of [relations with] an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא goes back to a later line of the same משנה and uses the ברייתא from step 4 on it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים reject רבי יהודה's rule against a bachelor herding, because ישראל are not suspected of these sins.

steps.title: New משנה: work that involves women
steps.stepSummary: A man whose business is with women may not be alone with women. A father should not teach his son a trade that is done with women.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Anyone whose work is with women may not be alone with women. A person should not teach his son a trade that involves women.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets two rules about men whose work brings them into contact with women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first rule is about יחוד, being alone together. A man who works with women may not be alone with them. The second rule tells a father not to steer his son into this kind of work at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He may not be alone with (יחוד)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Anyone whose business is with women
may not be alone with women,
and a person may not teach his son
a trade of women.
phrases.notes: He means a trade where a man deals with women all the time.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל שֶׁעֲסָקָיו עִם הַנָּשִׁים לֹא יִתְיַחֵד עִם הַנָּשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It continues the earlier topic of avoiding situations that could lead to sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who works with women may not be alone with them, and one should not teach his son such a trade.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: teach a clean, easy trade and pray
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says to teach your son a clean and easy trade and to pray to ה׳. Wealth and poverty do not come from the trade itself. Everything depends on a person's merit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: A person should always teach his son a clean, easy trade and pray to the One Who owns all wealth. Every trade has both poor people and rich people. Poverty does not come from the trade, and wealth does not come from the trade. Everything depends on a person's merit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives general advice about which trade to teach a son. He also explains where a person's living really comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since every trade has both rich and poor people, the trade does not decide how much a person earns. That depends on his זכות, his merit. So it makes sense to choose a clean, easy trade and rely on תפילה for success.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic Jewish outlook on making a living: do your part, but success comes from ה׳ according to merit.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
A person should always teach his son
a clean and easy trade,
and pray to the One to Whom wealth and property belong.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין אוּמָּנוּת שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ עֲנִיּוּת וַעֲשִׁירוּת,
phrases.english: For there is no trade that does not have poverty and wealth in it,
for poverty is not from the trade,
nor is wealth from the trade,
rather, everything is according to his merit.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם יְלַמֵּד אָדָם אֶת בְּנוֹ אוּמָּנוּת נְקִיָּה וְקַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה moves from which trade to avoid to which trade to choose.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teach a clean, easy trade and pray, because a living depends on merit, not on the trade.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: animals eat without work
steps.stepSummary: Animals and birds have no trade, yet they get their food without pain. People were meant to have the same, but they lost it through their sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: Have you ever seen a wild animal or a bird with a trade? Yet they get their food without pain. They were created only to serve me, and I was created to serve my Maker. Surely I should get my food without pain! But I made my deeds bad, and so I lost my easy living.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר brings a קל וחומר from animals. He uses it to explain why people must work hard for a living.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If animals, which exist only to serve people, get food without struggle, then people, who serve ה׳, surely should too. The fact that we struggle shows that something went wrong: our bad deeds took away an easy livelihood. This supports רבי מאיר's point that a living depends on merit.

keyTerms.meaning: They earn a living, get their food

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Have you ever in your days seen a wild animal or a bird
that has a trade?
Yet they get their food without pain!
And were they not created only to serve me,
while I was created to serve my Maker?
Is it not logical that I should get my food without pain?
But I made my deeds bad,
phrases.notes: 'I' here stands for people in general, not him personally.

phrases.english: and I cut off my livelihood.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָאִיתָ מִיָּמֶיךָ חַיָּה וָעוֹף שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם אוּמָּנוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a reason from nature that backs up רבי מאיר's idea that a living depends on merit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People were meant to earn a living without struggle, but lost this because of their sins.

steps.title: אבא גוריא: trades to avoid
steps.stepSummary: A father should not teach his son six trades: donkey driver, camel driver, potter, sailor, shepherd, and storekeeper, because these are trades of robbers.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא גוריין of צידן says in the name of אבא גוריא: A person should not teach his son to be a donkey driver, camel driver, potter, sailor, shepherd, or storekeeper, because their trade is a trade of robbers.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא גוריא lists six trades a father should not teach his son. He gives one reason for all six.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry here is not about women but about honesty. These trades easily lead to cheating or stealing, so they are called 'a trade of robbers.'

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּא גּוּרְיָין אִישׁ צַיְידָן אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם אַבָּא גּוּרְיָא:
phrases.english: Abba Guryan of Tzaydan says in the name of Abba Gurya:
A person may not teach his son [to be]
a donkey driver, a camel driver, a potter,
a sailor, a shepherd, or a storekeeper,
because their trade is a trade of robbers.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יְלַמֵּד אָדָם אֶת בְּנוֹ חַמָּר, גַּמָּל, קַדָּר, סַפָּן, רוֹעֶה, וְחֶנְוָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second group of trades to avoid, this time because of the risk of dishonesty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not teach a son trades that tend to lead to robbery.

steps.title: רבי יהודה rates the people in different professions
steps.stepSummary: In the name of אבא גוריא, רבי יהודה says most donkey drivers are wicked, most camel drivers are decent, and most sailors are pious. Even the best doctor goes to גיהנם, and even the most honest butcher is a partner of עמלק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says in his name: Most donkey drivers are wicked. Most camel drivers are decent. Most sailors are pious. The best of the doctors is headed to גיהנם, and the most honest of the butchers is a partner of עמלק.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה reports a different version of אבא גוריא's teaching. It does not lump all these trades together but judges each one separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike step 12, here camel drivers and sailors come out well, not badly. Only donkey drivers are called mostly wicked. Doctors and butchers are added with very strong warnings. The text does not say why.

keyTerms.meaning: עמלק, the enemy nation of ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה judges trades by the dangers that come with them: being alone with women, dishonesty, and moral risk. Above all, it teaches that a living really comes from merit and prayer, not from the trade itself.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this list up with step 12. In step 12, camel drivers and sailors are trades to avoid. In רבי יהודה's version, most of them are decent or even pious.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says in his name:
phrases.notes: 'His name' means אבא גוריא, from the step before.

phrases.english: Most donkey drivers are wicked,
and most camel drivers are decent,
most sailors are pious.
The best of the doctors is headed to Gehenna,
and the most honest of the butchers is a partner of Amalek.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשְּׁמוֹ: הַחַמָּרִין רוּבָּן רְשָׁעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of אבא גוריא's teaching, judging each trade separately.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Donkey drivers are mostly wicked, camel drivers mostly decent, sailors mostly pious, and doctors and butchers are judged very harshly.

steps.title: Teach your son only Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי נהוראי says he would set aside every trade and teach his son only תורה. תורה pays in this world and in עולם הבא, and it supports a person even when he is sick or old.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נהוראי says: I put aside every trade in the world and teach my son only תורה. A person eats from its reward in this world, and the main reward is saved for him in עולם הבא. Other trades are not like that. When a person gets sick, old, or suffers and cannot work, he starves. But תורה guards him from all evil when he is young and gives him a future and hope when he is old.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נהוראי gives the last opinion of the משנה about which 'trade' to teach your son. His answer is תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He compares תורה to an investment. You live off the 'interest' in this world, and the 'principal' stays safe for עולם הבא. Any other trade stops paying the moment you can no longer work, but תורה keeps protecting you at every stage of life.

keyTerms.meaning: The principal, the main sum (here: the main reward)

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי נהוראי goes further than רבי מאיר (Step 10). רבי מאיר advises a clean, easy trade together with prayer, while רבי נהוראי would set aside every trade and teach only תורה, which pays in this world and in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Nehorai says:
I set aside every trade in the world

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינִי מְלַמֵּד אֶת בְּנִי אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: and I teach my son only Torah,
for a person eats from its reward in this world,
and the principal stays for him for the World to Come,
and all other trades are not like that.
When a person comes to illness

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לִידֵי זִקְנָה אוֹ לִידֵי יִסּוּרִין,
phrases.english: or to old age or to suffering,
and he cannot work at his job,
he dies of hunger.
But Torah is not like that,
rather, it guards him from all evil in his youth,
and gives him a future and hope in his old age.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of opinions on which trade to teach a son, ending with the view that תורה is best.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teach your son תורה above all trades, because it supports him in this world, in עולם הבא, and in sickness and old age.

steps.title: Verses for youth and old age
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings a פסוק for how תורה protects a person in youth and another for how it supports him in old age.
steps.simpleTranslation: About his youth, what does the פסוק say? 'Those who hope in ה׳ will renew their strength.' About his old age, what does it say? 'They will still bear fruit in old age.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה backs up each half of רבי נהוראי's last line with a פסוק: one for youth and one for old age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Renew strength' fits youth, when תורה keeps a person strong against evil. 'Bear fruit in old age' fits old age, when other workers are finished but the תורה person is still productive.

phrases.english: About his youth, what does it say?
"Those who hope in ה׳ will renew strength."
About his old age, what does it say?
"They will still bear fruit in old age,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a פסוק for each part of רבי נהוראי's claim.
steps.raayaObject: That תורה protects in youth and gives hope in old age.

steps.title: אברהם kept the Torah and was blessed in old age
steps.stepSummary: אברהם אבינו was old and blessed in everything. That blessing came because he kept the whole תורה even before it was given.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says the same about אברהם אבינו: 'And אברהם was old… and ה׳ blessed אברהם in everything.' We find that אברהם אבינו kept the entire תורה before it was given, as it says: 'Because אברהם listened to My voice and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes, and My teachings.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a real-life example of the idea: אברהם אבינו, a keeper of תורה, was blessed in his old age. This closes the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First it shows that אברהם was blessed in old age. Then it proves he kept the whole תורה, so the blessing is linked to his תורה. The second פסוק lists many kinds of מצוות, which shows he kept all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: My charge, what I told you to guard

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends by showing that a life of תורה brings blessing even in old age, and אברהם אבינו is the model.

phrases.english: And so it says about Avraham our father:
"And Avraham was old...
phrases.notes: בראשית 24:1. The dots mean a few words of the פסוק are skipped.

phrases.english: and ה׳ blessed Avraham in everything" –
we find that Avraham our father kept

phrases.aramaic: אֶת כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִיתְּנָה,
phrases.english: the entire Torah before it was given,
as it says: "Because Avraham listened to My voice
and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes, and My teachings."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third proof, an example from a real person.
steps.raayaObject: That keeping תורה brings blessing in old age.

steps.title: Trades with women, and who cannot be appointed king or Kohen Gadol
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says anyone whose work is with women has bad ways, and lists such trades. It adds that we do not appoint people from these trades as מלך or כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Rabbis taught: anyone whose business is with women has bad ways. Examples are goldsmiths, wool-combers, millstone fixers, peddlers, weavers, barbers, launderers, the bloodletter, the bathhouse attendant, and the tanner. We do not appoint from them a מלך or a כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a ברייתא. It expands on the משנה's warning about trades that involve women and lists specific jobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate ideas here. First, workers who deal with women are often around them, so their ways are suspect. Second, people in these jobs (the list includes lowly ones like the tanner and bathhouse attendant) are not appointed to the highest positions, מלך or כהן גדול.

phrases.english: Gemara

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כׇּל שֶׁעֲסָקָיו עִם הַנָּשִׁים –
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: anyone whose business is with women –
his ways are bad,
phrases.notes: Literally 'his turning is bad.' He means his habits and the company he keeps are not good.

phrases.english: such as goldsmiths and wool-combers,
and millstone fixers and peddlers,
and weavers, barbers, and launderers,
and the bloodletter, the bathhouse attendant, and the tanner –
we do not appoint from them
neither a king nor a High Priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כׇּל שֶׁעֲסָקָיו עִם הַנָּשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens by expanding on the משנה's rule about trades done with women (Step 9).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Workers in trades with women have bad ways, and people from these trades are not appointed as מלך or כהן גדול.

steps.title: Why not appoint them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why these workers cannot be appointed as מלך or כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule it just quoted. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule could be read as saying these workers are halachically disqualified. The question opens the door to explain what the real problem is.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why people from these trades are not appointed as מלך or כהן גדול.

steps.title: Not disqualified, just a lowly trade
steps.stepSummary: The reason is not that these workers are unfit. Their trades are lowly, so they would not be respected in a high position.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not because they are disqualified, but because their trades are lowly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The problem is the low status of the job, not a halachic flaw in the person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מלך or כהן גדול needs the people's respect. Someone known for a lowly job would be looked down on, so he is not chosen, even though nothing about him is halachically wrong.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think these workers are sinners or halachically unfit. The גמרא says clearly that they are not disqualified. The only issue is the status of the job.

phrases.english: Not because they are disqualified,
but because their trades are lowly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The problem is the low status of the trade, not a disqualification of the person.

steps.title: Ten bad traits of the bloodletter
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists ten bad traits said about the גרע (bloodletter), from arrogance to being suspected of serious sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: ten things were said about a bloodletter. He walks sideways (proudly), he is arrogant, he leans when he sits, he is stingy, he is envious, he eats a lot and eliminates little, and he is suspected of forbidden relations, of stealing, and of bloodshed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that zooms in on one trade from the list, the גרע, and gives ten bad things said about him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ten traits fall into groups. Some are about pride (walking, attitude, sitting), some are about stinginess and envy, two are about how much he eats and how little he eliminates, and the last three are suspicions of the most serious sins: עריות, גזל and שפיכות דמים.

keyTerms.meaning: His spirit is coarse, he is arrogant
His eye is narrow, he is stingy
His eye is bad, he is envious

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עֲשָׂרָה דְּבָרִים נֶאֶמְרוּ בְּגָרָע:
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: ten things were said about a bloodletter:
he walks on his side, and his spirit is arrogant,
phrases.notes: 'Walks on his side' means he struts in a proud, showy way.

phrases.english: and he leans and sits,
and he is stingy, and he is envious,
he eats a lot and eliminates little,
and he is suspected of forbidden relations
and of stealing and of bloodshed.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עֲשָׂרָה דְּבָרִים נֶאֶמְרוּ בְּגָרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on one trade, the bloodletter, from the list in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bloodletter is described by ten negative traits, including being suspected of עריות, גזל, and שפיכות דמים.

steps.title: A father should teach his son a clean, easy trade
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא teaches that a person should always teach his son a trade that is clean and easy.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא taught: A person should always teach his son a clean and easy trade.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from בר קפרא with practical advice: pick a clean and easy trade for your son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the same words רבי מאיר used in the משנה (step 10), now taught by בר קפרא. After the lists of trades to avoid, the גמרא returns to the positive advice. It sets up the question of which trade actually counts as clean and easy.

phrases.english: Bar Kappara taught:
A person should always teach his son
a clean and easy trade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא brings בר קפרא, who repeats רבי מאיר's advice from the משנה (step 10). This sets up the question of which trade actually fits it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father should always teach his son a trade that is clean and easy.

steps.title: Which trade is clean and easy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which trade fits בר קפרא's description, and introduces רב יהודה, who will answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is such a trade? רב יהודה said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a real example of a clean and easy trade. It then names רב יהודה, setting up his answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר קפרא gave a general rule but did not name a trade. The גמרא wants a concrete example so the advice can actually be used. The words 'רב יהודה said' only open his answer; the answer itself comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (asking for a specific example)

phrases.english: What is it?
phrases.notes: He means: which trade actually counts as clean and easy?

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
phrases.notes: His answer comes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a concrete example of the general category בר קפרא described.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific trade counts as a clean and easy trade.
